catalog_quote: 5.2.4. Tone All six known languages in the Phowa clade feature a four tone system. For four of the six languages – Ani, Labo, Hlepho and Khlula – the system con- sists of contrastive high-level, mid-level, low-rising, and low-falling pitches. Zokhuo and Phukha follow this general pattern but lack a low-rising toneme. Instead, Zokhuo features a mid-high rising contour tone and Phukha features a high-mid falling contour tone (Fried 2000, Edmondson 2003). ... Further validation of the 4-tone (vs. 5-tone) system account is provided in the historical comparative account of tone system developments for Phowa clade languages in §6.4.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Khlula is described as a four-tone language (high-level /55/, mid-level /33/, low-rising /13/, low-falling /21/ on every syllable); the phonological sketch covering the Phowa clade has sections for syllable, initials, finals, tone and phonation only, and the book contains no statement about word stress or accent (full-text index: 0 hits for stress/stressed/prominence/rhythm).
new_statements.exceptions: Tone sandhi and initial-environment conditioning of pitch are mentioned for the clade (snippet: '..sandhi and/or initial environment. Further validation of the 4-tone (vs. 5-tone) system account is provided . §6.4'); nothing on stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Syllable-level lexical tone; statement is clade-wide (Phowa clade) with Khlula named explicitly; Khlula data from Pelkey's 2005-2006 wordlist elicitation at Laozhai (Wenshan Co., LZC) and Maxi (Maguan Co., MXC). Text seen only as Google Books full-text snippets, not as a saved page image.
new_statements.identity_note: Pelkey's Khlula data come from two datapoints: Khlula-LZC (Laozhai, Liujing Township, SE Wenshan County) and Khlula-MXC (Maxi community, Muchang/Renhe, Maguan County); both = khlu1236 [ykl]. The tone statement is made for the Phowa clade as a whole with Khlula named explicitly alongside Ani [ypn], Labo [ypb] and Hlepho [yhl] Phowa. In older Chinese sources the group appears as 'Tula' / Hei Phula / Shaoji Phula. Not to be confused with Wang Chengyou's 'Pula hua' of Kaiyuan (= Labo Phowa, labo1243).
